sections.text: When your project requires clean, precise holes through concrete, core drilling Spokane WA service from Northwest Concrete Cutting is the right call. Whether you're a plumber running drain lines through a basement slab, an electrician routing conduit through a concrete wall, or a contractor installing anchor bolts in a parking garage, core drilling Spokane WA delivers the accuracy and efficiency that impact methods simply can't match. We serve homeowners, general contractors, and industrial clients across Spokane, Spokane Valley, Liberty Lake, Cheney, and beyond—bringing professional diamond core drilling capabilities to projects of every size and scope.
What Is Core Drilling and When Is It Needed?

Core drilling is a controlled cutting method that uses a hollow, diamond-tipped drill bit to remove a cylindrical plug of concrete, masonry, or asphalt. The result is a smooth, precisely-sized hole with minimal vibration and no structural cracking in the surrounding material. Unlike hammer drilling or jackhammering, diamond core drilling preserves the integrity of the slab or wall you're working through—an important distinction on any project where the surrounding structure must stay intact. Core drilling Spokane WA contractors are called in whenever a penetration needs to be clean, accurately placed, and free of the collateral damage that impact methods cause. Common applications include plumbing sleeve installations, electrical conduit routing, HVAC duct penetrations, gas line installations, fire suppression system penetrations, anchor bolt placements, radon mitigation piping, and soil sampling for geological investigations. Core drilling is also used to create openings for elevator shafts, floor drains, and drainage sumps. Anywhere from a residential basement in the South Hill neighborhood to a commercial high-rise in downtown Spokane, diamond coring produces the kind of penetrations that allow trades to work cleanly without patching or repairing the surrounding concrete.
Drilling Diameters, Depths, and Project Types

One of the most important advantages of professional core drilling Spokane WA contractors is the range of hole sizes and depths they can achieve. Northwest Concrete Cutting operates diamond core bits ranging from 3/4 inch for small conduit penetrations up to 36 inches in diameter for large utility sleeves and drainage structures. Most residential and light commercial work falls in the 2- to 8-inch range, but our capabilities extend well beyond that for specialized applications. Depth capabilities vary by equipment setup and project requirements: shallow penetrations from 2 to 12 inches cover slab penetrations and anchor installations; mid-range depths from 12 to 36 inches handle wall penetrations, retaining wall tie-ins, and commercial floor work; and deep coring beyond 36 inches serves elevator pits, geological sampling, and deep utility routing. Our rigs handle both wet and dry core drilling methods. Wet drilling is the industry standard—water cools the diamond bit, extends its service life, and suppresses the silica dust that dry cutting generates. Dry drilling is reserved for situations where water damage is a concern, such as in occupied living spaces, near electrical equipment, or on projects where water runoff cannot be managed on site.
Diamond Core Drilling Equipment and Methods

Northwest Concrete Cutting uses professional-grade core drilling rigs built for high-demand commercial and industrial applications. Our diamond core bits are embedded with segments of industrial-grade diamonds that grind steadily through aggregate concrete, reinforced slabs, and hardened masonry without the cracking and spalling that chisel-based methods cause. We configure our equipment based on access requirements, material type, and production volume. Electric-powered rigs are used for indoor work in occupied buildings where exhaust fumes are not acceptable. Hydraulic rigs deliver maximum torque for large-diameter drilling through heavily reinforced concrete. Vacuum-mounted base setups handle slab work where anchor bolts are impractical, while anchor-mounted setups cover wall, ceiling, and overhead applications. Spokane's older building stock presents unique challenges: many structures built in the mid-20th century contain reinforcement that isn't documented in current drawings, and embedded utilities—electrical conduit, hydronic heating lines, post-tension cables—can be invisible from the surface. That's why Northwest Concrete Cutting strongly recommends pairing any core drilling Spokane WA project in an older or unknown structure with {{link:/services/concrete-scanning|GPR concrete scanning}} to locate rebar and utilities before the diamond bit touches the surface. Catching a post-tension cable or active conduit before drilling prevents costly damage and keeps your project on schedule.
Why Spokane's Freeze-Thaw Climate Demands Precision

Spokane sits at the crossroads of the Columbia Plateau and the Inland Northwest mountain ranges, giving the region one of the most punishing freeze-thaw environments in the Pacific Northwest. The city regularly logs over a hundred freeze-thaw cycles per winter season—nights dropping well below 32°F followed by daytime temperatures above freezing. Each cycle forces moisture inside the concrete to expand and contract, gradually widening micro-cracks and weakening the material over years. This is the reality that every Spokane concrete contractor lives with, and it shapes how penetrations need to be made. Any hole cut through a Spokane-area slab or wall needs to be done with this climate in mind. A rough or oversized core hole creates an immediate pathway for water intrusion. That water freezes and expands during cold snaps, accelerating the deterioration of the surrounding slab or wall far faster than normal aging would cause. Core drilling Spokane WA done correctly produces a tight, smooth opening that accepts grout or mechanical sleeves cleanly, sealing out moisture and extending the life of the penetration for decades. Contractors in Airway Heights, Cheney, and Spokane Valley all deal with the same conditions. Cutting clean penetrations isn't a nicety in Eastern Washington—it's a structural necessity driven by the region's demanding winters.
Commercial and Residential Core Drilling Applications

Core drilling Spokane WA projects span a wide range of industries and building types. On the commercial side, Northwest Concrete Cutting regularly works on office buildings and retail centers requiring floor-to-floor conduit paths and mechanical sleeves, industrial warehouses needing floor drain installations and equipment anchor pads, multi-level parking structures requiring drainage and electrical penetrations, healthcare and laboratory facilities where existing systems must be carefully avoided, restaurants requiring grease trap drain installations through thick slabs, and schools or government buildings undergoing renovation or seismic retrofits. Residential applications are equally common: basement bathroom additions requiring new drain lines through the slab, HVAC system retrofits in homes without existing duct penetrations, natural gas line routing through concrete foundation walls, radon mitigation system installations with sub-slab depressurization piping, deck anchor bolt installations through concrete pads, and crawl space access openings through perimeter foundation walls. Our {{link:/areas/spokane-wa/core-drilling|core drilling in Spokane}} team serves clients from Liberty Lake and Post Falls to Pullman and the heart of downtown. Whatever the project scope, we deliver {{link:/services/core-drilling|professional core drilling services}} that meet code, protect the surrounding structure, and hold up against the freeze-thaw stresses that are part of life in the Inland Northwest.
What to Expect During a Core Drilling Job

When you hire Northwest Concrete Cutting for core drilling Spokane WA work, the process follows a consistent, professional sequence designed to protect your structure and deliver accurate results. It starts with site assessment and layout: our crew reviews the project drawings, inspects the slab or wall, and marks every drill location precisely per your specifications. If there's any question about what's embedded in the concrete, we coordinate {{link:/services/concrete-scanning|a GPR concrete scan}} before drilling begins. Equipment is then set up appropriately for the application—vacuum-anchored to slabs for vertical drilling, bolt-anchored to walls for horizontal penetrations, or braced for overhead work. A water supply is connected for wet drilling setups and containment is placed to manage slurry runoff. During drilling, the diamond bit is run at controlled rotation and feed rates to maximize bit life and produce a clean bore. For larger-diameter openings, step-drilling with progressively larger bits may be used to maintain accuracy. Once complete, the cut concrete core is extracted and removed from the site, slurry is collected and disposed of properly, and the opening is prepared for whatever sleeve, grout, or fitting your project requires. The result is a precisely-located, clean-walled penetration ready for the next trade to work in without delay or remediation.
